entities.name: Operation Hailstone
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
Operation Hailstone was a pivotal 1944 United States naval operation during World War II, taking place in the Chuuk Lagoon on February 17, 1944. This event was a turning point in the Pacific Theater, marking a significant blow to the Imperial Japanese Navy's airpower and leading to the eventual Allied victory in the region.

The operation involved a combined force of American aircraft carriers and submarines, which launched a surprise attack on the Japanese naval base in Chuuk Lagoon. The attack resulted in the sinking of numerous Japanese ships and aircraft, as well as significant damage to the naval base and surrounding infrastructure.

The consequences of Operation Hailstone were far-reaching, contributing to the decline of Japanese naval power and paving the way for the Allied invasion of the Marshall Islands. The operation's impact was felt across the Pacific, shaping the course of the war and its ultimate outcome.

As Admiral Raymond Spruance, commander of the U.S. Fifth Fleet, noted, 'The destruction of the Japanese naval forces in the Carolines was a significant blow to their ability to wage war.'
